summary: SPAN destination oversubscribed: 2.52 Gbps mirrored from CORE-SW-01 Gi1/0/1 into 1 Gbps SPAN destination Gi1/0/48 causing 60.38% loss (16,328,520 of 27,042,840 packets discarded). NDR receives only 10,714,260 packets, severely degrading detection coverage.

findings.root_cause: CORE-SW-01 SPAN destination port Gi1/0/48 is oversubscribed and lossy by design. 2.52 Gbps of mirrored traffic from Gi1/0/1 is forced into a 1 Gbps SPAN destination (average load 100% of 1 Gbps, bursts higher). Switch discards excess on egress - 16,328,520 output discards, 60.38% loss. SPAN is best-effort copy with small buffers and drops under congestion, unlike a TAP.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR (requires both directions and full payload, 10 Gbps port) receives only ~39.6% of traffic. 60% random packet loss breaks flow reassembly, TCP stream reconstruction, and signature matching. Detections for lateral movement, C2, exfiltration will be missed and both-direction correlation fails.

recommended_fix.why: Physical TAP provides lossless, line-rate copy without SPAN oversubscription or CPU/buffer drops. Feed TAP via packet broker at 10G to match NDR's 10 Gbps tool port to eliminate the 2.52Gbps->1Gbps bottleneck and restore complete visibility.
